chapter_theme: The seventh part of Madurai Valaisami's Njanak Kummi lays out the Vedantic analysis of the great saying in three tiers of bodies, states and their owners. For the 'thou' (tvam-pada), the gross body in waking is owned by Visva, the subtle in dream by Taijasa and the causal in deep sleep by Prajna. For the 'that' (tat-pada), the Lord named omniscient, all-doer, inner controller and the rest takes the same three as Virat, Hiranyagarbha and Avyakrita, and his adjuncts are said to stain release. A third, Saiva tier follows: Siva's waking, dream and deep sleep (named world-devouring and upasanta) and Siva's turiya. Beyond all of them is the turiya that has not been seen, the form of Brahman-bliss, and the song ends on bowing to the feet of the guru whose form is that.
structure_note: The tvam-pada and its seven causes (2668 to 2670); Visva, Taijasa and Prajna with waking, dream and deep sleep (2671 to 2674); the tat-pada, its names and adjuncts (2675 to 2679); Virat, Hiranyagarbha and Avyakrita (2680 to 2682); the Siva-pada and its states, waking, the world-devouring dream, upasanta sleep and Siva-turiya (2683 to 2689); the turiya beyond, bliss and the guru's feet (2690 to 2692). The text of this part is badly corrupt in places; the readings follow the Vedantic scheme where the words allow, and the scheme is the tradition's, not something the stanza always spells out.

2668.reading: I will make known the tvam-pada, which is glory, and the adjuncts that came into it; hear what its nature is: the working of the conscious form told before, girl of knowledge.
2668.nuance: தொம்பதம் is the 'thou' of tat tvam asi, here the individual self considered with its உபாதி, limiting adjuncts. வசித்திரு is read as சித்துரு, the chit-form of 2667; the line is uncertain.

2669.reading: The body full of vasanas, the prana breath, the senses joined as one, and the mind with the rest that grew together: these are the causes, girl of knowledge.
2669.nuance: வாசனை (latent impressions), body, prana and the senses are listed with மதி and its fellows; காசலையா is unclear. The next stanza counts the list as seven, which suggests body, prana, senses and the four inner faculties, but the stanza does not name them all.

2670.reading: These seven called causes came and mingled with the tvam-pada; in the turiya of the causal tvam-pada they became its own body, girl of knowledge.
2670.nuance: The claim is that what the self takes as its body is the seven adjuncts mingled with it. அரியத்தில் is read as துரியத்தில், turiya, the fourth state; the syntax is loose.

2671.reading: The self that holds the gross waking as its own is afterwards named Visva, by its identification, girl of knowledge.
2671.nuance: In the Vedantic scheme விஸ்வன் (Visva) is the self identified with the gross body in waking. அபிமானம், owning or identifying, is the operative word: the names belong to the identification, not to the self.

2672.reading: Joined with the adjuncts that bear names, the subtle comes in dream, and the name of the one who stands in it is Taijasa, girl of knowledge.
2672.nuance: சைதனாம் is read as தைசதன் (Taijasa), the owner of the subtle body in dream; the stanza is corrupt in lines 1 and 3.

2673.reading: When prana with its breaths subsides and is joined to the root, and the gathered nada-turiya is joined, that is the causal body.
2673.nuance: The causal body is described in yogic terms, breath withdrawn into the root and the nada reached, rather than in the textbook terms of ignorance; the stanza lacks the refrain and may be damaged.

2674.reading: The state joined is deep sleep, and the one who joins it is Prajna; bow to the one who has seen all three keenly, and dance the kummi.
2674.nuance: பிராக்ஞன் (Prajna) owns the causal body in deep sleep, completing the triad Visva, Taijasa, Prajna. கண்டராமத்தை is read as 'the one who saw' the three, the witness; it may be a corrupt or punning word.

2675.reading: Having bowed and seen the settled meaning of the tvam-pada, by the same rule I will now tell the discrimination of the tat-pada, girl of knowledge.
2675.nuance: சித்தார்த்தம், settled meaning, and விவேகம், discrimination, are the method: each pada is analysed by stripping its adjuncts, and the same procedure is turned on 'that'.

2676.reading: What is to be known? As the tvam-pada thing had its adjuncts, so for the all-pervading thing of the tat-pada there are its own body, its jiva and its turiya.
2676.nuance: The parallel is the point: the Lord too has adjuncts, a body and states, so 'that' as ordinarily named is no less conditioned than 'thou'. சருவதற்பா is read as சர்வ தற்பதம்.

2677.reading: The omniscient, the all-doer, the inner ruler of all, the lord of all, the creator of all, the preserver of all and the destroyer of all are its names, girl of knowledge.
2677.nuance: Seven Sanskrit epithets of Isvara (sarvajna, sarvakarta, sarvantaryami, sarvesvara, and creator, preserver and destroyer of all). Calling them 'names' prepares the next stanza's charge that they are adjuncts.

2678.reading: What are these names? Spoken at length these seven are turiya; but because it took on adjuncts that do not yield, a fault has come upon release, girl of knowledge.
2678.nuance: தூஷணம், fault or blemish, is the striking word: the Lord's own attributes, as adjuncts, count against liberation, so the 'that' must be stripped as the 'thou' was. Line 2 (வாதம் தரியமடி) is corrupt.

2679.reading: The faulted jiva, having seen these seven, became the body of the one they name; because it is called the eternal place, its name is the shadow-grasp, girl of knowledge.
2679.nuance: சாயாகிரகம் may be the reflection (chaya) of 2611, the jiva as Brahman's reflection, or a corrupt word; பானுக்கு is unclear (the sun, or பரனுக்கு, 'for the Supreme'). The reading is tentative.

2680.reading: Calling the waking oneself, and beyond it the one who owns it: the wise will name him Virat; know it, girl of knowledge.
2680.nuance: விராட்டன் (Virat) is the cosmic counterpart of Visva: the Lord identified with the gross universe in its 'waking'. காமர் is probably a misprint for the wise or the learned.

2681.reading: The three adjuncts known, and joined in them, it is the supreme dream; the inseparable owner of it they call Hiranyagarbha, girl of knowledge.
2681.nuance: இரணியகர்ப்பன் (Hiranyagarbha) is the cosmic counterpart of Taijasa, owner of the subtle universe as 'dream'. பர சொப்பனம், supreme dream, marks it as the Lord's state, not the jiva's.

2682.reading: With one part of this, for the Supreme there is a deep sleep; the one who joins it, see in your mind, is called Avyakrita, girl of knowledge.
2682.nuance: வியாகிருதன் is read as அவ்யாகிருதன் (Avyakrita, the unmanifest), the cosmic counterpart of Prajna; 2610 named the same three, Avyakrita, Hiranyagarbha and Virat, from the top down. பார்சுழித்தி is read as பர சுழுத்தி.

2683.reading: See: as the meaning of the tat-pada was seen and known, hear the truth of the Siva-pada of knowledge, girl of knowledge.
2683.nuance: Having done 'thou' and 'that', the kummi adds a third pada, Siva's, which is the Saiva extension of the Vedantic scheme found in Tirumular (the third, Siva's turiya). சிவகாதத்தி is read as சிவபதத்தின்.

2684.reading: Having seen the true supreme turiya, but by the fault of not seeing it to the end, the Supreme became the body of the pure one of the cool Siva-pada, girl of knowledge.
2684.nuance: The pattern repeats: each tier's 'body' is the tier below seen incompletely. Here even the Supreme (பரன்) serves as the body of Siva, the pure one, so that Siva stands above the Isvara of the tat-pada.

2685.reading: The supreme world-devouring and the upasanta, which are spoken of: for the Siva who has practised one of these three kinds, there is the supreme waking, girl of knowledge.
2685.nuance: விஸ்வகிராசம், 'devouring the universe', and உபசாந்தம், quiescence, are names for Siva's states, the world absorbed and the stillness beyond it. பர சாக்கிரம், supreme waking, is the first of Siva's states. The grouping 'one of three' is unclear.

2686.reading: The one who owned the Siva-waking, which is the thing that comes to be, is Siva-turiya, gathered; so the saying declares, girl of knowledge.
2686.nuance: Line 3 (சேகரமாயிடிறசிறசொலிதையென்று) is garbled and the stanza is read only in outline: the வாக்கியம், the great saying, is said to declare the owner of Siva's waking.

2687.reading: The saying is the world-devouring; the Siva-dream that is the path of bondage, and its fortunate owner, they call Prajapati; say it, girl of knowledge.
2687.nuance: பிரசாபத்தன் may be Prajapati or a corrupt name; the source has a dash in the line. Calling Siva's dream பந்த மார்க்கம், the path of bondage, is odd and may be corrupt.

2688.reading: And what is told as upasanta is the Siva deep sleep; if one stays in it, he is the good and graceful one called Santa; is that not desire, girl of knowledge?
2688.nuance: The final question, அது காமம் அல்லவோ, turns on the scheme itself: resting in Siva's deep sleep as a 'peaceful one' is still a wish. It echoes the litany of ஆசை in 2657 to 2661.

2689.reading: In the named Siva-turiya, losing identification and standing alone, is that not the true welfare? They have not seen the state of the first turiya, girl of knowledge.
2689.nuance: அபிமானம் இழந்து தனித்து, losing the sense of owning and standing alone, is the sign of the last tier: no one owns this state. ஆதி துரியம், the first or primal turiya, which 'they have not seen', leads into the next stanza's turiya beyond.

2690.reading: What has not been seen is the complete turiya; seeing it and whirling, it is the highest; bow to the ancient form of Brahman-bliss and dance the kummi.
2690.nuance: முற்றிரியம் is read as முற்றுத் துரியம், the complete turiya, or turiyatita, beyond all three tiers. சுழன்று, whirling, may be the dance of the kummi or the whirl of the central channel.

2691.reading: This is the knowledge bowed to; this is the supreme bliss; look boldly, worship the one whose form is bliss, and dance the kummi.
2691.nuance: After the analysis the stanza turns to praise; துணிந்து பாரு, 'look boldly', asks for a direct seeing rather than more counting.

2692.reading: The happy jiva to be worshipped and the pure supreme thing are this; is this not the foot of the flawless guru whose form is the Self, girl of knowledge?
2692.nuance: The identity the whole analysis sought, jiva and supreme thing as one, is finally located at the guru's foot, a pun the kummi also makes in 2693 (பாதம், foot, and பதம், word). சொரூபக் குரு is the guru who is the Self.

links.note: This part opens the analysis of the tvam-pada and its adjuncts; the last part closes it by saying the 'thou' became the foot that is the 'that', with all differences, adjuncts and states become it. The adjuncts counted here are what 2693 dissolves.

Tirumular says that when the seven causal adjuncts are gone the true Supreme is the 'that' of bodhanta; Valaisami lists seven names of the Lord and calls them adjuncts that stain release. Both make 'that' as well as 'thou' something to be stripped.

In 2610 the kummi named Avyakrita, Hiranyagarbha and Virat with consciousness above them; here it explains them as the Lord's owners of waking, dream and deep sleep, matched to the jiva's Visva, Taijasa and Prajna.

Tirumular lists after the supreme waking a dream that has eaten the world, deep sleep and upasanta, and makes reaching them the bearing of Siva's turiya; Valaisami names the same set, supreme waking, the world-devouring and the upasanta, as Siva's states. The kummi is following the Tirumanthiram's Saiva extension of the avasthas.

Tirumular distinguishes the soul's turiya, the Supreme's turiya and Siva's turiya and matches them to tvam, tat and asi; Valaisami's three tiers end the same way, with the jiva's states, the Lord's states and Siva's turiya in which identification is lost.

Both place the goal past turiya itself: the other verse says 'beyond even turiya, far, far, far'; Valaisami calls it the turiya never seen, above all three tiers of states, and names it Brahman-bliss.

source_issues: 2668: முன் சொன்னவசித்திரு is unclear, perhaps சித்துரு.
2670: அரியத்திற் is probably துரியத்தில்; தொம்பத்ததைத் doubles a letter.
2671: போல்லோ is garbled; the stanza ends with a stray comma.
2672: சைதனாம் is probably தைசதன்; lines 1 and 3 are damaged.
2673: வாயுவடன் for வாயுவுடன்; the stanza ends தேகமடி without the refrain and may be incomplete.
2678, 2683: ஞானப்பெண்னே for ஞானப்பெண்ணே; 2678 line 2 (வாதம் தரியமடி) is corrupt.
2679: பானுக்கு and சாயாகிரகம் are doubtful; the stanza ends with a stray comma.
2682: வியாகிருதன் for அவ்யாகிருதன்; பார்சுழித்தி for பர சுழுத்தி.
2684: தன்னுடலாச்சுக has a stray final letter.
2687: the line contains a stray dash (பத்தனென் - சொல்).
2689: the stanza ends with a stray comma.
